page_title: Barzilai-Borwein Fails Superlinear Convergence on an Open Set of Quadratics for Every Dimension $n\geq 4$
subject: Barzilai-Borwein method
statement: The paper proves the Barzilai-Borwein method does not converge superlinearly for almost every strictly convex quadratic problem and initialization.

page_title: Barzilai-Borwein Fails Superlinear Convergence on an Open Set of Quadratics for Every Dimension $n\geq 4$
subject: Barzilai-Borwein method
statement: The paper shows that for dimension $n\geq4$, the long Barzilai-Borwein method (BB1) converges on an open family of strictly convex quadratic problems where every spectral component of the gradient is bounded by corresponding geometric sequences, ruling out superlinear convergence.

page_title: Encoding Invisible Causation for Bridge Diagnostic Agents: Triple-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning with QLoRA
subject: Damage Cause Encoder
statement: The paper proposes a Damage Cause Encoder that classifies 10-class damage causes from visible damage descriptions for use in autonomous bridge diagnostic agents.

page_title: Encoding Invisible Causation for Bridge Diagnostic Agents: Triple-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning with QLoRA
subject: Damage Cause Encoder
statement: The Damage Cause Encoder chains Knowledge Triple Extraction from 15-35 diagnostic PDF manuals indexed in FAISS with retrieval-augmented context at training and inference time.

page_title: Encoding Invisible Causation for Bridge Diagnostic Agents: Triple-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning with QLoRA
subject: QLoRA
statement: The paper reports QLoRA achieves 87.07% test accuracy on the Golden Testset (116 stratified samples).

page_title: Encoding Invisible Causation for Bridge Diagnostic Agents: Triple-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning with QLoRA
subject: QLoRA
statement: The paper reports QLoRA achieves identical test accuracy to full-precision LoRA with 11% faster inference, 72% lower GPU memory, and superior generalization across unseen inputs.

page_title: Encoding Invisible Causation for Bridge Diagnostic Agents: Triple-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning with QLoRA
subject: QLoRA
statement: The paper reports QLoRA outperforms LoRA by 13 percentage points on a 100-sample diverse evaluation spanning all 10 damage cause classes.

page_title: Evaluation design conditions the expert-vs-auto MeSH gap: a controlled comparison of bag-of-words and BiomedBERT on the Cohen benchmark
subject: bag-of-words classifier
statement: The paper reports the bag-of-words classifier's expert-vs-auto MeSH gap on Statins is +0.096 WSS@95% under the canonical 5-fold full-corpus design on the Cohen benchmark.

page_title: Evaluation design conditions the expert-vs-auto MeSH gap: a controlled comparison of bag-of-words and BiomedBERT on the Cohen benchmark
subject: bag-of-words classifier
statement: The paper shows the bag-of-words classifier's expert-vs-auto MeSH gap reduces to +0.033 (95% CI includes zero) when matching corpus size to smaller topics (n=803) on the Cohen benchmark.

page_title: Evaluation design conditions the expert-vs-auto MeSH gap: a controlled comparison of bag-of-words and BiomedBERT on the Cohen benchmark
subject: bag-of-words classifier
statement: The paper reports the bag-of-words classifier's expert-vs-auto MeSH gap reduces to +0.021 (CI narrowly excludes zero) under 10-fold cross-validation at full Statins corpus size.

page_title: Evaluation design conditions the expert-vs-auto MeSH gap: a controlled comparison of bag-of-words and BiomedBERT on the Cohen benchmark
subject: BiomedBERT
statement: The paper reports BiomedBERT's expert-vs-auto MeSH gap is +0.020 on Statins, within sampling noise of the bag-of-words 10-fold result.

page_title: Evaluation design conditions the expert-vs-auto MeSH gap: a controlled comparison of bag-of-words and BiomedBERT on the Cohen benchmark
subject: BiomedBERT
statement: The paper reports 15.1% of Statins inputs exceed BiomedBERT's 512-token limit when expert MeSH terms are appended, potentially affecting classification performance.

page_title: An Introduction to Bayesian and Frequentist Simulation-Based Inference with Machine Learning
subject: neural posterior estimation
statement: The paper describes how neural posterior estimation can be used for parameter estimation within Bayesian and frequentist statistical frameworks for simulation-based inference.

page_title: Prior laundering: learned priors with inherited, undetectable overconfidence
subject: learned generative priors
statement: The paper shows learned generative priors trained on archive of legacy reconstructions inherit overconfidence where measurements are uninformative, with uncertainty reporting the archive's belief rather than the data's.

page_title: Prior laundering: learned priors with inherited, undetectable overconfidence
subject: learned generative priors
statement: The paper shows averaging the legacy posterior over measurements yields the old regularizer advanced a single expectation-maximization step, explaining the inherited overconfidence.

page_title: Prior laundering: learned generative priors with inherited, undetectable overconfidence
subject: diffusion prior
statement: The paper demonstrates that a diffusion prior fit to the archive under-covers the operator's blind subspace compared to a truth-trained control baseline.

page_title: Prior laundering: learned generative priors with inherited, undetectable overconfidence
subject: normalizing flow
statement: The paper reports a normalizing flow fit to the archive similarly under-covers on a nonlinear groundwater operator, exhibiting inherited overconfidence.

page_title: Deep Sigma Point Processes for RCS Modeling in Spaceborne SAR Imagery
subject: Deep Sigma Point Processes
statement: The paper introduces Deep Sigma Point Processes that use a hierarchical Gaussian process framework with Bayesian inference to predict RCS in synthetic aperture radar imagery.

page_title: Deep Sigma Point Processes for RCS Modeling in Spaceborne SAR Imagery
subject: Deep Sigma Point Processes
statement: The paper reports Deep Sigma Point Processes achieve 20.83% reduction in root mean squared error compared to linear regression baselines on RADARSAT-2 test data with 208,191 verified ships.

page_title: Deep Sigma Point Processes for RCS Modeling in Spaceborne SAR Imagery
subject: Deep Sigma Point Processes
statement: The paper reports Deep Sigma Point Processes achieve 25.89% increase in R-squared compared to linear regression baselines on RADARSAT-2 test data.

page_title: Deep Sigma Point Processes for RCS Modeling in Spaceborne SAR Imagery
subject: Deep Sigma Point Processes
statement: The paper reports Deep Sigma Point Processes achieve 44.4% reduction in both residual interquartile range and median absolute deviation on the RADARSAT-2 test data.

page_title: Humanly: A Configurable and Traceable Environment for Human-AI Collaborative Writing
subject: Humanly
statement: The paper introduces Humanly, a writing platform that records writing activity and in-platform AI assistance for personal documents or assigned tasks.

page_title: Humanly: A Configurable and Traceable Environment for Human-AI Collaborative Writing
subject: Humanly
statement: The paper proposes that Humanly can package a completed session into a sealed writing certificate with configuration-aware anomaly behavior review.

page_title: Humanly: A Configurable and Traceable Environment for Human-AI Collaborative Writing
subject: Humanly Typing Detector
statement: The paper reports a red-teaming study shows the Humanly Typing Detector distinguishes human hand typing from automated typing.

page_title: Humanly: A Configurable and Traceable Environment for Human-AI Collaborative Writing
subject: Humanly
statement: The paper reports a user study shows Humanly is helpful across roles including course assignments, peer review, and personal certification.

page_title: Reliability-Aware Bayesian Optimization of 1310 nm PCSELs with FDTD Verification
subject: reliability-aware Bayesian optimization
statement: The paper couples a commercial finite-difference time-domain solver to a reliability-aware Bayesian optimization loop over eight local design variables for PCSEL design refinement.

page_title: Reliability-Aware Bayesian Optimization of 1310 nm PCSELs with FDTD Verification
subject: reliability-aware Bayesian optimization
statement: The paper reports that across three 80-evaluation runs, reliability-aware Bayesian optimization produced 5-15 candidates per run that passed the joint wavelength and beam-quality filter.

page_title: Reliability-Aware Bayesian Optimization of 1310 nm PCSELs with FDTD Verification
subject: reliability-aware Bayesian optimization
statement: The paper reports designs from reliability-aware Bayesian optimization retained Q_eff=4.33×10^6-7.76×10^6, a 60-108-fold increase over baseline metric, at 1308.23-1310.90 nm with ~0.84° divergence.

page_title: Reliability-Aware Bayesian Optimization of 1310 nm PCSELs with FDTD Verification
subject: reliability-aware Bayesian optimization
statement: The paper reports reliability-aware Bayesian optimization gave the highest mean strict-filter yield (9.0 candidates) compared with differential evolution (7.0) and Latin-hypercube sampling (1.5) under equal budgets.

page_title: Agentic Evaluation of Copyright Law Compliance
subject: Copyright-Bench
statement: The paper introduces Copyright-Bench, a benchmark comprising realistic commercial tasks including website development, merchandise design, and pitch deck production.

page_title: Agentic Evaluation of Copyright Law Compliance
subject: LLM agents
statement: The paper reports that comparing state-of-the-art LLM agents against a human baseline, agents select copyrighted works despite the availability of public-domain alternatives.

page_title: Agentic Evaluation of Copyright Law Compliance
subject: LLM agents
statement: The paper reports that for open-weights LLM agent models, violation rates increase in response to certain user preferences and simulated time pressure.

page_title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
subject: StARS
statement: The paper proposes StARS, reformulating socially appropriate action generation as a preference modelling problem inspired by recommender systems.

page_title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
subject: StARS
statement: The paper proposes StARS integrates collaborative filtering with learnable scene representations to generate user-specific appropriateness scores.

page_title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
subject: StARS
statement: The paper presents StARS as model-agnostic, capable of integration with various scene encoders and backbones enabling personalisation without redesigning the underlying model.

page_title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
subject: StARS
statement: The paper reports StARS consistently improves performance and agreement with annotators across MannersDB+ and SocNav1 datasets.

page_title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
subject: StARS
statement: The paper makes StARS code publicly available at https://github.com/Cambridge-AFAR/StARS.git.

page_title: Data eccentricity, asymptotics of Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and kernel PCA
subject: Gaussian RBF kernel
statement: The paper shows that, up to isotropic scaling, the Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space is asymptotically isometric to Euclidean space in the large bandwidth limit.

page_title: Data eccentricity, asymptotics of Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and kernel PCA
subject: Gaussian RBF kernel
statement: The paper shows Gaussian RBF eigenvalues, eigenprojections, and principal components all converge to those of classical (linear) PCA as bandwidth σ→∞.

page_title: Data eccentricity, asymptotics of Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and kernel PCA
subject: Gaussian RBF kernel
statement: The paper shows RKHS feature embeddings and orthogonal PCA eigenframes of Gaussian and linear kernels differ asymptotically by a geometric similarity transformation with residual O((ρσ)^2), where ρ measures data eccentricity.

page_title: Data eccentricity, asymptotics of Gaussian RBF reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and kernel PCA
subject: data eccentricity
statement: The paper reports data eccentricity ρ (ratio of maximum to median pairwise distance) provides a simple and reliable predictor of dataset-specific convergence behavior in top principal directions.

page_title: A Graph-Based Control Interface for Traffic Signals on Heterogeneous Road Networks
subject: graph neural network traffic control
statement: The paper presents a traffic-signal control interface where a shared graph neural network assigns scores to individual traffic movements and junctions convert these into legal signal phases.

page_title: A Graph-Based Control Interface for Traffic Signals on Heterogeneous Road Networks
subject: graph neural network traffic control
statement: The paper describes movement nodes representing controlled input-to-output paths and typed mean aggregation producing one scalar per movement, with phase definitions outside the learned network.

page_title: A Graph-Based Control Interface for Traffic Signals on Heterogeneous Road Networks
subject: graph neural network traffic control
statement: The paper reports PPO-trained policies retained performance across unseen geometries within the synthetic grid family.

page_title: A Graph-Based Control Interface for Traffic Signals on Heterogeneous Road Networks
subject: graph neural network traffic control
statement: The paper reports a single trained city-policy instance executed across all five city graphs, with heterogeneous outcomes on unseen road networks.

page_title: ToolGuardian: Declarative Security for AI Agent-Tool Interactions
subject: ToolGuardian
statement: The paper presents ToolGuardian using progressive characterization to convert evidence into structured facts through descriptions, system-call traces, mock execution, and source analysis.

page_title: ToolGuardian: Declarative Security for AI Agent-Tool Interactions
subject: ToolGuardian
statement: The paper introduces ToolGuardian's core contribution as an Answer Set Programming (ASP)-based declarative policy layer that reasons over capabilities, effects, task context, and composition.

page_title: ToolGuardian: Declarative Security for AI Agent-Tool Interactions
subject: ToolGuardian
statement: The paper reports that for vetting 16 MCP-style tools including 8 malicious variants, ASP reaches a deny-class F1 of 0.86 and 88% accuracy using description, syscall, and observed-effect evidence.

page_title: ToolGuardian: Declarative Security for AI Agent-Tool Interactions
subject: ToolGuardian
statement: The paper reports that for runtime authorization on 20 scenarios, fully specified ASP realizations classify all scenarios correctly.

page_title: Quantifying Political Partisanship for Cross-Platform Analyses
subject: partisanship measurement methodology
statement: The paper proposes a text-based methodology embedding posts using a transformer-based sentence encoder and clustering into topic groups labeled by aggregated news credibility scores.

page_title: Quantifying Political Partisanship for Cross-Platform Analyses
subject: partisanship measurement methodology
statement: The paper constructs a partisanship axis in embedding space as the difference between centroids of oppositely labeled clusters, with individual posts scored by projection onto this axis.

page_title: Quantifying Political Partisanship for Cross-Platform Analyses
subject: partisanship measurement methodology
statement: The paper reports partisanship scores correlate significantly with held-out AllSides media bias scores both in-distribution and out-of-distribution on an independent Twitter corpus.

page_title: Quantifying Political Partisanship for Cross-Platform Analyses
subject: partisanship measurement methodology
object: applied to 1.3M posts from Bluesky/Truth Social
statement: The paper applies the methodology to approximately 1.3 million posts from Bluesky and Truth Social during the six months preceding the 2024 U.S. presidential election.

page_title: SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes
subject: SCALE
statement: The paper proposes SCALE, a framework with a self-supervised layout-generation stage that learns to reconstruct randomly masked polygons from BEOL context without violation labels.

page_title: SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes
subject: SCALE
statement: The paper fine-tunes a domain-adapted DRC vision-language model providing rule-aware geometric guidance for local DRV repair in SCALE.

page_title: SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes
subject: SCALE
statement: The paper reports SCALE boosts state-of-the-art agents' DRV solve rates by +12-25% (up to 97%) on 100 real sub-2nm test cases spanning enclosure, spacing, width, and color-spacing violations.

page_title: Data Quality over Capacity: Internalizing Documents into LoRA Adapters for Closed-Book QA
subject: LoRA
statement: The paper reports that across roughly 100 training runs, training-data quality is the dominant lever on closed-book accuracy, outweighing LoRA rank, learning rate, and two alternative architectures combined.

page_title: Data Quality over Capacity: Internalizing Documents into LoRA Adapters for Closed-Book QA
subject: LoRA
statement: The paper reports that a single curation pass on a 15-document corpus moved closed-book accuracy from 57.7% to 85.7%, a larger jump than any architectural change.

page_title: Data Quality over Capacity: Internalizing Documents into LoRA Adapters for Closed-Book QA
subject: LoRA
statement: The paper reports the internalized LoRA adapter (84.2% recall) beats a BM25-RAG pipeline with base reader (58.9%) and a gold-chunk oracle (65.6%) at lower latency on a 15-document slice.

page_title: Multi-Agent System-driven Digital Twins for predictive maintenance: architectures, technologies and open research challenges
subject: Multi-Agent Systems and Digital Twins
statement: The paper establishes a taxonomy of existing hybrid Multi-Agent and Digital Twin architectures for predictive maintenance in resource-constrained industrial contexts.

page_title: Multi-Agent System-driven Digital Twins for predictive maintenance: architectures, technologies and open research challenges
subject: Multi-Agent Systems and Digital Twins
statement: The paper identifies persistent technological bottlenecks in deployment of Multi-Agent Systems with Digital Twins based on analysis of over 547 papers in high-impact journals.

page_title: Remedying Coarsening-Based GNN Training under Heterophily via Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
subject: Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
statement: The paper proposes Adaptive Complementary Enhancement (ACE), a plug-and-play strategy that reconstructs original node features and applies anisotropic structural regularization to embed local heterophily.

page_title: Remedying Coarsening-Based GNN Training under Heterophily via Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
subject: Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
statement: The paper adopts homoscedastic uncertainty weighting in ACE to adaptively balance the training objective of coarsened-graph loss and full-graph auxiliary loss with augmented node features.

page_title: Remedying Coarsening-Based GNN Training under Heterophily via Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
subject: Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
statement: The paper reports ACE drives consistent gains on heterophilic benchmarks while preserving competitive results on homophilic graphs with minimal computational overhead.

page_title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
subject: level-appropriate conversational agent
statement: The paper reports that 87.4% of dialogue sentences generated by the proposed multi-agent system fell within one predicted CEFR level of the learner's self-assessed proficiency.

page_title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
subject: level-appropriate conversational agent
statement: The paper reports 87.4% for the level-appropriate agent compared to 54.1% for the unsimplified agent in producing dialogue at the learner's proficiency level.

page_title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
subject: level-appropriate conversational agent
statement: The paper reports that a preliminary pilot study with Japanese university students did not yield statistically significant evidence that the system reduces foreign language anxiety levels, likely due to small sample size.
